answer_summary: q1 merge buildout YES (done); q2 merge editor YES (done); q3 PROD HOLD until after walkthrough; q4 BYOK-only forever (no hosted pool; Claude Max for agent-driven testing); q5 Damien test-drives editor then sends John's link; q6 walkthrough ~Wed 2026-07-23 (tentative); q7 BUILD ALL fast-follows this weekend. main = platform v0 + editor, DEV-deployed, PROD held.
summary_html:
Two ships are built and green — the only real gate is one API key

The platform build-out and the editor experience are both done, tested, and DEV-proven. Nothing here is hard-blocked except that a single model API key is what unlocks the live demo (red-team gate, live client interview, optional hosted pool). Everything else in this form is a go/no-go or a scheduling call you can answer in one sitting.

  • Ship & merge: two feature branches ready for main; PROD deploy is a hold-or-go call.
  • The API key: the one blocker — which provider, and where you will store it.
  • John's editor: when to hand John his magic link, and when to schedule the John & Roger walkthrough.
  • Fast-follows: multi-select which enhancement to build next (recommendation: none until after the walkthrough).

Recommended options are pre-selected. PROD deploys and provider keys always come back to you regardless — this form is the durable record of the call.

questions.topic: Provide a model API key — unlocks the demo
questions.context_html:
This is the single real gate. One key unlocks three things, each one command: the live red-team gate (D3/D4 probes), the live client interview in the walkthrough, and — optionally — the hosted demo pool ($10/day cap already enforced server-side).

  • Anthropic (recommended): prompt-caching on the ≥4096-token persona prefix makes it ~$0.055/interview.
  • OpenAI / Google: supported via the same provider-agnostic BYOK adapters; no caching economics.
  • BYOK-only forever: no hosted pool — every user pastes their own key; the demo still runs, you just paste yours each session.
  • Note field: tell me where you'll put it (e.g. ~/.secrets/…) — keys are never stored or logged, BYOK is source-scan-tested.

Links: demo runbook (🔑 steps) · deferred-gate notes

questions.topic: Send John his magic edit link now, or test-drive it yourself first?
questions.context_html:
John's tokens are staged in ~/.secrets/sonsteng-editor-tokens (never printed, never committed). Building his URL and sending it is a 2-minute step whenever you say go.

  • Recommended: you spend ~10 minutes in the editor yourself first, guided by the one-page John guide, then send — so you've seen exactly what he'll see.
  • Or send now: the queue is expected empty; John starts suggesting immediately.
  • Either way safe: everything John does is a suggestion — nothing goes live without your accept + the validator parity gate.

Links: editor guide for John · "Handing John his link"
